title: Introduce retrospective audit stitcher and tenant KMS consent synchronizer
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We observed gaps in late-arriving audit events and KMS consent state when services replayed historical data after cluster restarts or cross-region repairs. This PR introduces two coordinated components: 1) a retrospective audit stitcher that consumes audit event fragments, reconstructs canonical operation traces, and writes verified audit envelopes to the audit ledger; and 2) a tenant KMS consent synchronizer that reconciles consent assertions from external KMS providers and emits deterministic residency-aware consent events used by RBACv2 policy decisions. Together these address incidents where audit timelines diverged from KMS consent state and improve forensic completeness. || What this does: - Adds services/audit/retrospective_stitcher service (Go) with a pluggable input backend (Kafka/Blobstore) and deterministic envelope builder. - Adds services/kms/consent_synchronizer (Go) to perform periodic reconciliation, backfill missing consent events, and emit signed consent-assertions to the audit bus. - Extends rbac decision path with a lightweight consent cache and a new consent_verifier middleware used by policy-evaluator. - Adds migration tooling to reprocess a configurable lookback window and a one-off job to retroactively stitch the last 30 days of audit fragments. - Adds observability: new metrics, tracing spans, and labels for tenant/region pin provenance. || Notable implementation notes: - The stitcher uses HMAC-based chunk ordering to avoid reliance on eventual ordering guarantees from the input queues; integrity checks reject replays older than the configured watermark. - The synchronizer supports multiple KMS providers via a provider interface; the initial implementation includes AWS KMS and a noop shim for on-prem HSMs. - To avoid policy regressions during rollout, the consent cache is read-through and supports TTL-based soft-fallback while the synchronizer warms up. - Security: signed audit envelopes include a key-id header; consent events include residency evidence metadata (region-pin and telemetry hash). || Rollout plan: 1) Deploy stitcher and synchronizer in canary region with audit-only mode (no policy enforcement) for 48h. 2) Enable RBACv2 consent_verifier middleware in read-only mode to surface mismatches in tracing/metrics. 3) After validation, enable enforcement behind a kill-switch and gradual traffic ramp. 4) Run retro-stitch backfill job on production ledger with rate-limits; monitor ingestion backpressure and KMS API quotas. || Related: ENG-4921 (consent reconciliation), SEC-731 (audit completeness), SUP-2148 (customer incident: missing consent in cross-region failover).

b9f1e22: implement chunk ordering and envelope builder with HMAC verification
c7a2d11: add consent_synchronizer provider interface and aws_kms provider
d3e6f9a: integrate consent cache into rbacv2 policy-evaluator middleware
e4f7b66: add migration job: audit_stitch_backfill and CLI flags
f1a3c8b: add metrics/tracing, dashboard dashboards, and alert rules

review_comments: Jonah Park: Please add an explicit proof of idempotency on the backfill job; replaying the same window should be a no-op. - Addressed in commit e4f7b66, added idempotency marker and dry-run flag.

Luis Romero: How does this interact with existing audit retention compaction? We should ensure we don't resurrect trimmed fragments. - Reply: stitcher skips fragments older than retention threshold and logs a soft-failure metric; added a WARN-level trace when fragments are missing.

Ellen Strauss: KMS quotas are a concern for large tenant fleets. Can we batch consent queries and add exponential backoff? - Reply: implemented batched provider lookups with per-tenant rate buckets and jittered backoff; see providers/aws_kms.go commit.

Security review (automated): Ensure envelope signatures are added and key rotation accounted for. - Action: envelope_builder signs with env-key and key-id header; key rotation handled via key registry lookup.
QA: Found a race in the consent cache TTL refresh under high concurrency; added sync.Once guard and a unit test covering concurrent refresh.
ci_summary: CI initially failed lint on envelope_builder.go (style) and a flaky e2e test; lint fixed and e2e retried — all checks pass (unit, integration, e2e in sandbox, security-scan: SCA ok).
release_notes: Adds a retrospective audit stitcher to reconstruct and canonicalize fragmented audit events and a tenant KMS consent synchronizer to reconcile consent state across providers. Includes migration tooling to backfill recent history and new RBACv2 consent verification middleware. Rollout behind feature flags; non-breaking by default.
notes_for_ops: Operators: new Helm values (retrospectiveStitcher.enabled, consentSynchronizer.syncInterval, consentSynchronizer.batchSize). Backfill job cli: tools/migrations/audit_stitch_backfill --lookback=720h --dry-run. Watch metrics: audit.stitcher.missing_fragments, kms.consent.reconcile_errors, rbac.consent.cache_hit_rate.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Run dry-run backfill in staging and validate ledger diffs. 2) Schedule canary deployment for 48h. 3) Coordinate with SRE to monitor KMS quotas and set alert thresholds. 4) Add runbook entry under runbooks/audit-stitcher.md.
marketing_context: This change improves audit completeness guarantees and customer-facing compliance controls by ensuring consent provenance is visible and reconcilable across failures — valuable for enterprise customers with strict residency and auditability requirements.
